newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa rallies on stg, bullish crop report.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa rallies on stg, bullish crop report.

text.p: London cocoa futures staged a fierce rally in late dealings on Tuesday on sterling's retreat from highs, finishing above the key technical barrier of 943 stg basis March.

Traders said prices were fuelled also by a report by UK cocoa analysts PCR Ltd forecasting the 1996/97 world cocoa supply deficit at 127,000 tonnes compared with an estimated surplus of 186,000 tonnes in the previous season.
"The market went up on sterling. Then everybody piled in to cover shorts," said one trader.

The benchmark March position gained a hefty 23 stg on the day to end at 944 stg a tonne. It was just off its session high of 945 stg but closed above the technically-important 943 stg which was the high last week.
Traders said London's performance was technically bullish as prices formed an "outside day reversal" which means they had a lower low and a higher high than the previous session.
The day's turnover reached 9,139 lots, mainly clustered on the second month March.
PCR's estimate was based on an Ivorian output forecast of 1.065 million tonnes for 1996/97 compared with 1.220 million seen in 1995/96.
Total world production was pegged at 2.695 million tonnes, significantly lower than last season's estimate of 2.929 million and grindings were up by three percent at 2.795 million.
PCR said cocoa prices were due for a correction, mainly as the stocks/consumtion ratio was expected to narrow to a 10-year low of 39 percent from 44 percent in 1995/96.

Although the PCR report was seen bullish, traders were puzzled as it came in just hours after a report by the Economist Intelligence Unit (EIU) which put the cocoa deficit at 20,000 tonnes in 1996/97.
"These numbers are wildly different. Nobody knows what to make of these," said one trader.
"But PCR is quite well respected in the cocoa market so I expect it might have had an influence," he added.
Traders cited some manufacturer scale-down buying in London amid a spate of trade and speculative short covering.
In late currency dealings sterling eased to $1.6375 from around $1.6699 in the morning.
The outgoing Dec structure was trading at a discount of 60 stg a tonne against the benchmark March, traders said.
Technically, London is expected to encounter resistance at 955 stg and 968 stg on March.
